:::{#thm-mixture-two-stage}
#### A mixture is the density of a two-stage random variable

Let $C$ be a discrete random variable
and $X$ a continuous random variable
with [joint density-mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-joint-density-mass)

$$\p(C = c,\, X = x) = w_c \, {\p_c}(x), \quad c \in \set{1, \ldots, K},$$

with ${\p_c}$ and $w_c$ as in @def-mixture.
Then:

- $\P(C = c) = w_c$,
- for each $c$ with $w_c > 0$,
  the [conditional density](expectation.qmd#def-cond-mixed) of $X$ given $C = c$ is ${\p_c}$, and
- the mixture ${\p_{\text{mix}}}$ is a density of $X$.

:::

::: proof

By the [marginal PMF from a joint density-mass function](random-variables.qmd#cor-joint-density-mass-marginal),

$$
\begin{aligned}
\P(C = c) &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} w_c \, {\p_c}(x)\,dx \\
&= w_c,
\end{aligned}
$$

because ${\p_c}$ is a density and so integrates to 1.
Then, by the [definition of the conditional density](expectation.qmd#def-cond-mixed),

$$
\begin{aligned}
\p(X = x \mid C = c) &= w_c \, {\p_c}(x) / w_c \\
&= {\p_c}(x).
\end{aligned}
$$

For the last claim, the events $\set{C = 1}, \ldots, \set{C = K}$
are mutually exclusive, and their union is the whole sample space.
So for any interval $B$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(X \in B)
&= \sumto{c}{K} \Pr(C = c,\, X \in B)
&& \text{(additivity over the events } \set{C = c} \text{)} \\
&= \sumto{c}{K} \int_B w_c \, {\p_c}(x)\,dx
&& \text{(definition of a joint density-mass function)} \\
&= \int_B \sumto{c}{K} w_c \, {\p_c}(x)\,dx
&& \text{(a finite sum of integrals is the integral of the sum)} \\
&= \int_B {\p_{\text{mix}}}(x)\,dx
&& \text{(definition of a mixture)}
\ea
$$

And ${\p_{\text{mix}}} \ge 0$, as a sum of non-negative terms,
so ${\p_{\text{mix}}}$ is a [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) of $X$.

:::
